name: Paharpur
note: Somapura Mahavihara: UNESCO inscription in 1985.

name: Shat Gombuj Mosque · Historic Mosque City
note: A fifteenth-century mosque associated with Khan Jahan at Bagerhat. It is a principal monument within the UNESCO-listed Historic Mosque City of Bagerhat.

name: Sundarbans
note: Mangrove ecosystems connect biodiversity, coastal livelihoods and storm protection; UNESCO inscription in 1997.

name: Mahasthangarh
note: Ancient Pundranagara: a key archaeological anchor for early Bengal.

name: Mainamati
note: Buddhist archaeological remains include Shalban Vihara.

name: Wari-Bateshwar
note: Early settlement and trade are important archaeological study themes.

name: National Martyrs' Memorial
note: Savar's memorial commemorates the martyrs of the Liberation War.

name: Mujibnagar
note: The provisional government's oath-taking site, 17 April 1971.

name: Sonargaon
note: Historic urban heritage and Jamdani traditions connect this area to Bengal's textile history.

name: Shilaidaha
note: Kuthibari is associated with Rabindranath Tagore.

name: Kaptai Lake
note: A reservoir linked to hydropower, fishing and displacement of hill communities.

name: Tanguar Haor
note: A Ramsar wetland; northeast haors face pre-monsoon flash-flood exposure.

name: Hakaluki Haor
note: A major northeastern wetland supporting fisheries and bird habitats.

name: Lawachara
note: Forest biodiversity and conservation in the northeastern tea-growing region.

name: Madhupur tract
note: An elevated terrace with sal forests; forest-dependent livelihoods and land-use change matter here.

name: Barind tract
note: An elevated terrace where dry-season water management is an important theme.

name: Kuakata coast
note: A coastal study anchor for tourism, cyclone preparedness and shoreline change.

name: Nijhum Dwip
note: An estuarine island associated with coastal afforestation and wildlife habitat.

name: Halda River
note: An important natural carp-spawning river; water quality and habitat protection matter.

name: Padma Bridge
note: Inaugurated on 25 June 2022; connects the southwest with the capital region.

name: Chattogram port
note: A major maritime trade gateway on the Karnaphuli.

name: Mongla port
note: A southwestern seaport on the Pasur river system.

name: Bagha Mosque
note: An early-sixteenth-century Sultanate mosque at Bagha. Its brickwork and terracotta panels are key examples of Bengal mosque ornamentation.

name: Kusumba Mosque
note: A stone-faced mosque at Manda, built in 1558–59 during Afghan rule. Its carved mihrabs and raised prayer gallery distinguish the monument.

name: Chhota Sona Mosque
note: A Sultanate mosque in the Bangladesh part of Gaur, built during the reign of Alauddin Husain Shah. Its stone ornament and formerly gilded roof gave it the name Small Golden Mosque.

name: Darasbari Mosque
note: The ruins of a large Gaur mosque built by Yusuf Shah in 1479. Its terracotta decoration and nearby madrasa connect worship with the history of learning.

name: Atiya Mosque
note: An early-seventeenth-century mosque at Delduar combining Sultanate and Mughal features. Terracotta panels and a curved cornice are its memorable details.

name: Star Mosque (Tara Masjid)
note: An Armanitola mosque dating from the first half of the nineteenth century. Later chini-tikri mosaic decoration and blue star motifs gave the mosque its familiar name.

name: Khan Muhammad Mridha Mosque
note: A Mughal mosque in Lalbagh dated by inscription to 1704–05. Its three-domed prayer hall stands on a raised terrace with vaulted rooms below.

name: Goaldi Mosque
note: A single-domed Sultanate mosque at Sonargaon, dated to 1519 by its inscription. Stone and terracotta mihrab decoration survive in the restored building.

name: Suhrawardy Udyan
note: Formerly the Ramna Racecourse, this ground is associated with the 7 March 1971 speech and the Pakistani military surrender on 16 December 1971. It is a major independence-history study location.

name: Ramna Park
note: A long-established public park in central Dhaka with mature trees and a lake. It belongs to the wider historic Ramna landscape and is distinct from nearby Suhrawardy Udyan.

name: Bahadur Shah Park
note: An Old Dhaka park formerly known as Victoria Park. Its memorial connects the site with the uprising of 1857 and the memory of the last Mughal emperor.

name: Baldah Garden
note: A historic botanical garden in Wari established by Narendra Narayan Roy Chaudhury in 1909. Its two sections are called Cybele and Psyche.

name: Chandrima Udyan
note: A park beside Crescent Lake, north of the National Parliament complex. The grounds include the mausoleum of former president Ziaur Rahman.

name: Lalbagh Fort
note: An unfinished Mughal fort begun in 1678. The surviving ensemble includes a mosque, the tomb of Pari Bibi and a Diwan-i-Aam with a hammam.

name: Ahsan Manzil
note: The former residence of the Dhaka nawabs beside the Buriganga. Its nineteenth-century palace and dome are important landmarks in the history of Old Dhaka.

name: Kantajew Temple (Kantanagar)
note: An eighteenth-century temple famous for detailed terracotta scenes from epics and everyday life. Its original nine spires were lost in the earthquake of 1897.

name: Panam City
note: A historic merchant settlement within the wider Sonargaon area. Its surviving street-front houses reflect nineteenth- and early-twentieth-century trade and architecture.

name: Puthia Rajbari and temples
note: A palace and temple ensemble at Puthia. The Rajbari, Govinda Temple and Shiva Temple make this an important location for studying zamindari patronage and Bengal architecture.

name: Tajhat Palace
note: A historic palace at Tajhat, Rangpur, with a broad central stair and imposing frontage. The building houses the Rangpur museum.

name: Uttara Ganabhaban (Dighapatia Palace)
note: The former palace of the Dighapatia rulers near Natore. The palace grounds and buildings preserve a major example of the region’s zamindari heritage.
